Upgrade the atlases an atlas package ships

Source: R/atlas_upgrade.R
upgrade_atlas_package.Rd

Rewrites every atlas in a package's R/sysdata.rda through ggseg.formats::as_ggseg_atlas(), which brings it to the current object representation and schema. Nothing is recomputed: no source volume is read, no surface is projected, no geometry is touched. The atlas comes out with the same core table, the same palette and the same geometry it went in with, in the shape the installed ggseg.formats expects.

Usage

upgrade_atlas_package(path = ".", dry_run = TRUE, repair = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Path to the atlas package. Defaults to the working directory.

dry_run

If TRUE (the default), report what would change and write nothing.

repair

If TRUE, run the migration verbs on an atlas the current constructor refuses, and upgrade the result. Off by default: a repair changes stored data, where an upgrade does not. Some published atlases need it – ggsegAal's .aal3_cerebellum carries the pre-vocabulary hemi value "middle" and no verb that validates will touch it.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with one row per atlas object: its name, the schema it carried, the schema it now carries, and whether its contents verified identical.

Details

This is deliberately not a rebuild. Re-running a package's data-raw scripts reruns the pipeline, which picks up every pipeline fix since the atlas was last built and is not output-identical – the MCALT cerebellar atlas changed eight labels the last time it was rebuilt, and label is the key every user's data joins on. Upgrading changes the container; rebuilding changes the contents. Do them as separate pieces of work, so that when something moves you know which one moved it.

It also works for packages that cannot be rebuilt at all: those whose source volumes were never committed, or whose build script points at a machine that is not yours.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# See what would change
upgrade_atlas_package("~/workspace/ggseg/atlases/ggsegSchaefer")

# Do it
upgrade_atlas_package(
  "~/workspace/ggseg/atlases/ggsegSchaefer",
  dry_run = FALSE
)
} # }
